question: Haven, 5v5, 50s. Your team is split between A and C. You are Sova at Mid/Window with Recon Bolt, Owl Drone, Shock Bolt. How do you use your util to settle the decision?

options.label: Fire a Recon Bolt scanning A Link / A Short to count the DEF on A before your team commits
options.explication_courte: The Recon reveals how many DEF are on A - the exact information that resolves the A vs C debate cleanly without committing your body.

options.label: Send the Owl Drone into Mid/A Link for a live scan and a potential dart, before deciding
options.explication_courte: The Drone gives richer positional info (exact locations) but immobilizes you and makes noise; a valid option but costs more time and exposes your drone.

sources_option.citation: Drones give richer live info than a recon dart but immobilize the user and make noise, telegraphing intent and exposing the pilot.

options.label: Throw a Shock Bolt onto a common A angle to deal damage, without scanning first
options.explication_courte: A blind Shock Bolt without info spends a damage charge for a random result; you learn nothing about the site count and solve nothing.

sources_option.citation: Before throwing utility ask what information it gives and what you'll do differently; damage util thrown blind, without a read, is reactive and low-value.

options.label: Hit A immediately without any info util, assuming A is the weaker site based on feel
options.explication_courte: Committing on an unchecked assumption when you have a full Sova info kit wastes every tool he has and converts an informed decision into a forced guess.

sources_option.citation: Top players process incomplete information under time pressure; committing to a site on assumption when you have recon tools available wastes your read.

explication_longue:
Situation: Haven, 5v5, 50 seconds. Your team is debating A vs C (Haven has 3 sites - information is king). You are Sova at Mid/Window with Recon Bolt, Owl Drone, Shock Bolt.

Core mid-round principle: information before commitment. Haven's three-site structure makes reading the DEF split critical - hitting the wrong site against 3 stacked defenders is a losing execute. Sova's Recon Bolt is designed for this: one bolt through A Link/A Short counts the defenders and tells you definitively whether A is contested or stacked.

If the Recon shows 1-2 DEF on A, hit A; if 3+, pivot to C. The Owl Drone (acceptable) gives richer positional info but immobilizes you and makes noise. The Shock Bolt (costly) burns damage without answering the player count question. Committing without any scan (mistake) turns a solved information problem into a 50/50 guess despite having the tools to solve it for free.

Estimated elite distribution: ~55% Recon Bolt first then commit, ~22% Owl Drone scan, ~16% Shock Bolt (costly), ~5% blind commit (mistake).

sources.citation: Before throwing any utility the key question is what information it gives and what you'll do differently; if you can't answer, you're using it reactively.
Good executes compress defender decisions by using info tools first; recon reveals how many defenders sit on a site so you hit the weaker one.
In-game leaders interpret rotations and stack tendencies under time pressure; information gathering precedes commitment.

_gaps.incertitude: Recon Bolt (optimal) vs Owl Drone (acceptable) : le choix depend du setup DEF exact et de la ligne de recon disponible depuis Window ; si l'angle recon est bloque, le drone monte en priorite. Ligne non encodee.
Estimations depuis guides mid-round/execute (theguide, boosteria, idsnews) ; pas de dataset sur la frequence recon-first vs drone-first par elo en elite.
Positions x/y approximatives sur Mid/Window Haven (viewBox 1000x1000, zones maps.ts) ; le spot exact du Recon Bolt (ligne A Link) n'est pas encode dans le JSON.
